item.title: Watch the complete Blacktalons saga in one epic supercut
item.description: Enjoy over three hours of intense Warhammer animation.
item.content:encoded:
Neave Blacktalon – one of Sigmar’s greatest Stormcast assassins – has a fractured past that even she can’t piece together. Now you can watch her rediscover her memories across the entire animated saga Blacktalon in one mammoth supercut.

This epic tale clocks in at a mighty 3 hours and 36 minutes long, featuring gripping fights, deadly betrayals, and winding intrigue as Neave and her team battle Nurgle’s corruption* across the Mortal Realms. 

All the while, Neave’s missing memories plague the back of her mind, and a looming shadow watches her struggle with malevolent interest.

Whether you’re grabbing a bowl of popcorn to watch Blacktalon: Final Cut in one marathon sitting or putting it on in the background while you paint up your own Stormcast Eternals, it’s well worth a watch, and some of the best storytelling Warhammer TV has to offer.

Watch it now with a Warhammer+ subscription, alongside hundreds of other episodes of animations, game shows, lore videos, painting tutorials, and more.

item.title: Aly Morrison
item.content:encoded:
We are deeply saddened to hear news of the passing of Aly Morrison.

Aly was a pioneering miniatures designer, whose creativity and talent helped shape Warhammer as we know it across five decades. From Dwarfs to Giants, Space Marines to the Red Gobbo – his imagination and craftsmanship have inspired generations of collectors, painters and gamers. 

Aly’s kindness and generosity as a mentor have left an indelible mark on the Warhammer Studio. Humble, magnanimous and with an incorrigible wit, to sit beside Aly and hear his wisdom and love of Warhammer miniatures design, was to be in the presence of a master. No matter your level of experience, he always had something insightful to add, to help make the creation ‘more Warhammer’.

Our thoughts and condolences are with Aly’s family, friends and all who had the privilege of working alongside him. 

Blessed with a warm and mighty heart, Aly had time for everyone: a friendly smile and a genuine greeting were his hallmarks. He will be sorely missed.

item.title: The Adepta Sororitas make their presence known in Warhammer 40,000: Darktide
item.description: Step into the boots of a Novitiate in an upcoming DLC.
item.content:encoded:
The citizens of Tertium have prayed for deliverance, and now the God-Emperor provides as the Sisters Novitiate will join Warhammer 40,000: Darktide as a new playable class.

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

Play as one of the pious Sisters Novitiate and flood the hive with faith and fire in a new DLC launching on 7 December, alongside a free update adding the iconic meltagun to the Novitiate and Veteran classes. 

The Sister Novitiate plays unlike any of the classes released so far, as rather than blitz and combat abilities they may choose any two of six Acts of Faith to unleash against the heretic hordes, powered by their accumulated Faith. Exactly how you generate that Faith depends on your talent tree choices, with several Devotions and Pledges available to customise your play style.

And what an arsenal they’ve brought to mete out the God-Emperor’s punishment – alongside the aforementioned meltagun, Novitiates can also wield the condemnor stake thrower, Ministorum hand flamer, mace of the righteous, penitent eviscerator, and Novitiate sword and shield – plenty of tools for splattering heretics in all manner of ways.

The new Sister Novitiate DLC will be available on Steam, PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S from 7 December.

item.title: Seminars, signings, and merch – Black Library Live returns
item.description: Coming to Warhammer World this December.
item.content:encoded:
Black Library Live returns to the home of Warhammer this December as part of the 30th anniversary of Warhammer World.

Buy Your Ticket

Black Library Live is the celebration of Warhammer fiction – a great day out for regular readers of Warhammer stories and fans of the lore. It’s another reason (as if any were needed) to make the trip to Warhammer World as it marks its 30th anniversary.

This event is your chance to meet and hear from the authors behind some of your favorite Black Library books. The day will include signings and seminars, and a preview where you’ll be the first in the world to hear about some upcoming Black Library titles.

Authors confirmed so far:

  • John French

  • Jude Reid

  • Gav Thorpe

  • Robbie MacNiven

  • Victoria Hayward

  • Guy Haley

  • Robert Rath 

A dedicated Black Library Live shop will be open to all customers at Warhammer World on the day, and Black Library Live ticket holders will get exclusive early access.*

This event will also be the first time anywhere in the world that you can get your hands on the signed and numbered Mega Edition of The Horus Heresy: Dropsite Massacre – ticket holders will have a guaranteed opportunity to buy a copy. This edition will also be available at other events in 2027, and a limited quantity will be available at the Black Library Live store on the day available to purchase for non-ticket holders.

You can also grab a copy of the new illustrated and annotated edition of Cypher: Lord of the Fallen by John French – who will be at the event!

There will also be a range of rare and limited edition titles available on the day.

Alongside the books will be a selection of Black Library and Warhammer merch, including special t-shirts.

Tickets are £30 and get you full access to the event including seminars, previews and author signings, as well as entry to the Warhammer World exhibition. Warhammer World will also be open as usual – so even if you miss out on a ticket (and we are expecting them to sell fast) you can still head down to the shop and the Black Library Live store, grab some of the books and merch on sale, and enjoy the gaming hall, exhibition and Bugman’s Bar.

Tickets for Black Library Live are on sale right now. Grab yours today:

item.title: New Core Mission Pack for Warhammer: The Horus Heresy
item.description: Discover fresh ways to play in the Age of Darkness.
item.content:encoded:
Warhammer: The Horus Heresy is getting a new Core Mission Pack and the Legiones Astartes are getting new Primary Detachments. Here’s the team behind the game explaining the different ways you can now play.

Warhammer: The Horus Heresy Team: Hot on the heels of the updated FAQ document last month we have produced a new series of Core Missions. These are intended to be used in a similar manner to the Core Mission pack found in the Age of Darkness Rulebook, but include several new elements based on the feedback we have received.

The first is that this Mission Pack includes three Primary Objective types, allowing players to score victory points for controlling objective markers, controlling sectors of the battlefield, or simply destroying enemy units. As well as providing an interesting variety of challenges for players to overcome, these also help provide a taste of the kinds of variation that can be found in the Mission Packs in the various Journal Tactica supplements. Two of these Primary Objectives now also have the option to be played using the Escalation or Hammerblow variants, allowing players to either score victory points at the end of each turn, or only at the end of the battle, a format which will be familiar to players of previous editions of the game.

These missions also include more potential deployment maps and are played for more turns than many other Mission Packs, allowing players much more variety. Plus, Vehicle and Cavalry units are able to score Objectives in these Missions! This means you can lean into more unusual army archetypes when preparing for your battles.

Speaking of army building, we have also created a range of new alternative Primary Detachments available to Legiones Astartes armies, reflecting some popular army builds from the past. These include the Veteran and Terminator-centric Pride of the Legion, the massed Dreadnoughts that make up the Fury of the Ancients, the swift and deadly antigrav craft of the Sky-Hunter Phalanx and the deadly vehicles of the Armoured Spearhead (did we mention that Cavalry and Vehicles can more easily interact with victory conditions in the new Core Missions?). Each of these provides a number of benefits, providing appropriate bonuses as well as a series of restrictions.

Also included is a brand-new Primary Detachment designed to accurately represent the protocols and methodology of Legiones Astartes Orbital Assaults. Alongside the usual benefits and restrictions, this utilises an all-new deployment method, designed to allow players to recreate the devastating effectiveness, as well as inherent risk, of committing their forces to an orbital drop assault into the midst of an enemy force!

Thanks folks! The new Core Mission Pack and Primary Detachments are available to download for free now.

item.title: Meet the Khazalite Ancestor Gods
item.description: Who exactly are the duardin swearing oaths to?
item.content:encoded:
The Ancestor Gods are a pretty big deal in Khazalite culture, showing up in both their army rules and prayer lores – but before you start swearing oaths or chanting prayers, make sure you know exactly who you’re beseeching for aid.

The duardin of the Khazalite Holds believe their eight gods were once mortals, and though some are older than others, all hold equal veneration in the hearts of honest, goodly Khazalites. All but one…

Grungni – The Father God

Grungni is the most respected of all the Ancestor Gods, renowned for his great deeds, including forging lightning for Sigmar himself. The Khazalites understand that Grungni wants to see their scattered clans united, based on his mantra that the duardins’ path will only hold if it is forged through unity.

Valaya – The Mother Goddess

A symbol of fortitude and healing, fortress builders honour her as protector of duardin holdings, and brewers revere her as the patron of all ales. In ancient days, her shield spared Karak Thryngaz from immolation, and cleansed the waters of Strufsson’s Tarn, saving its breweries.

Gazul – The God of the Underworld

The Stonebeard guides the dead on their final journey to his Gate, and through his runic mastery their souls are kept safe from the clutches of Nagash. His watch is endless, standing vigil against quiet undead and horrors of Chaos alike.

Grimnir – The God of the Axe and Battle

Known as the Fearless, Grimnir represents the warrior spirit of the duardin. The Fyreslayers believe that, despite falling in battle against the godbeast Vulcatrix, some part of his spirit endures.

Grombrindal – The White Dwarf

Old Whitebeard, the Wanderer – there isn’t a duardin who doesn’t know the legends of Grombrindal. An ever-roaming wayfarer and rememberer of places, Grombrindal guides the duardin in their search for lost karaks.

Thorgrim – The Grudgebearer

Stern as iron, Thorgrim remembers every ill deed and wrong perpetrated against the duardin, adding them to 

his Great Library of Grudges. He embodies the vengeful side of the duardin, hoarding the grudges of an entire race so that they do not consume their souls.

Inghilde – The Delver

The youngest of the pantheon, Inghilde’s intrepid spirit inspires the duardin to prospect and mine deep beneath the earth’s surface. She is the patron goddess of miners and stonesmiths, and, like Grombrindal, represents the pioneering spirit of the duardin – him above ground and her below.

Hashut – The Fallen God

Shorn from the pantheon, his statues rubble and his name a curse, Hashut is the fallen God who brings shame to all duardin. When any hope of redemption was lost, it was Valaya who struck him down.

Find out more about the Ancestor Gods, and the wider Khazalite Holds, when their battletome goes up for pre-order this Saturday, alongside their new miniatures.

item.title: Bring Khazalite might to armies of Order with Regiments of Renown
item.description: Duardin resilience is a hot commodity in the Mortal Realms.
item.content:encoded:
For such a stubborn lot, the duardin of the Khazalite Holds work rather well with their Grand Alliance Order allies, and two new Regiments of Renown from their upcoming battletome show you how.

Fjori’s Vengeance

The first, Fjori’s Vengeance, stars the last survivor of Guzanhold and the gaggle of mercenary Fyreslayers he’s gathered to help him wreak ancestral retribution upon those responsible for the magmahold’s fall. As a Grimhold Exile, Fjori is a deadly close combat killer who can normally propel himself to a distant board edge once per game, but now with the Regiment’s new Itinerant Grimmdron rule he can bring the rest of his gang with him too.

ITINERANT GRIMMDRON

Once Per Battle (Army), Deployment Phase

Well used to being outnumbered, Fjori turns the situation to his advantage as he outflanks the foe with his warriors.

Effect: If the Grimhold Exile in this Regiment of Renown has used the ‘Wrathful Wanderer’ ability this battle, remove the other units in this Regiment of Renown from the battlefield and set them up again on the battlefield wholly within 6" of a battlefield edge, wholly within 6" of the Grimhold Exile in this Regiment of Renown and more than 9" from all enemy units. Then, give a unit in this Regiment of Renown 1 grudge mark.

The sudden appearance of tough and dangerous Fyreslayers is a great help to many armies who want to pull enemy troops away from the front line, as it’s pretty hard to ignore someone with the potential to throw out Damage 3 attacks when charging.

Grimhold Exiles are accustomed to operating alone. They go where they will, and death follows them.

Effect: Remove this unit from the battlefield, then set it up again on the battlefield wholly within 6" of a battlefield edge and more than 9" from all enemy units.

His entourage are equally dangerous and the whole lot can appear from any point near a board edge – great for teaming up with soaring Kharadron Overlords airships or speedy aelven cavalry.

Thengin’s Grudgesettlers

The second Regiment of Renown brings a spot of duardin rune magic to other Order armies courtesy of the eponymous Runewright and his contingent of hardy Khazalite infantry. It’s a sizable force compared to its Grimmdron peers, with 10 Clanshields, 10 Clangunners, the Runewright himself, and an Oathkeeper Cannon to keep enemy heads down.

This Regiment of Renown doubles down on the hardiness of the average duardin and is perfect for less durable armies* who want a hard core to brawl over tricky objectives. The Rune of Stoicism spell is a great little buff that will help your forces stick around a bit longer with Ward 6+, while the Grudgesettlers rule gives them a hefty punch early in the game by starting with an ever-useful grudge token.

RUNE OF STOICISM (7)

Your Hero Phase

The sombre resonance of this rune instils in duardin a stubborn determination.

Declare: Pick the Runewright in this Regiment of Renown to cast this spell, then make a casting roll of 2D6.

Effect: Until the start of your next turn, units in this Regiment of Renown have WARD (6+) while they are wholly within 12" of and visible to this unit.

Keywords: SPELL

GRUDGESETTLERS

Passive

No matter the grievance, Thengin and his kin are ever ready to mete out retribution.

Effect: Each unit in this Regiment of Renown starts the battle with 1 grudge mark.

If a unit in this Regiment of Renown destroys an enemy unit, you must remove the grudge mark from that friendly unit.

This Regiment of Renown is also a particularly nice way to get some of the lovely new Khazalite Holds miniatures even when you’re not planning to start a full army, as they can be used across the whole spectrum of Grand Alliance Order armies. You get a cannon! We bet the Daughters of Khaine or Idoneth Deepkin would love to have a cannon handy.

Will you be adding a wandering band of hard-headed Khazalites to your army? The Khazalite Holds go on pre-order from Saturday, including Fjori’s Vengeance and the individual units that make up Thengin’s Grudgesettlers.

* Aelves, we’re looking at you here.

item.title: The Warhammer 40,000 Updates Update
item.description: A Warhammer 40,000 rules log is incoming.
item.content:encoded:
You may have noticed that the October rules update for Warhammer 40,000 didn’t appear in your app as a single smooth release. Instead, it arrived as sporadic downloads over several days.

This is our bad.

We’re sorry for any confusion this caused. We’re going to do better. Here’s Adam to explain further:

Can't see this video?

This video is hosted on a third party website, which may be using cookies. To see it, you need to accept cookies by clicking on the button below. You can change your preferences at any time by clicking Cookie Settings at the bottom of any Warhammer Community page.

New Rules Update Log – coming with the next update

As Adam said in the video above, alongside the next version of the Warhammer 40,000 app, Warhammer Community is going to host a Rules Update Log to help explain the changes in simple terms. This log will list a summary of any rules changes along with date stamps to make it easy to track, which we hope will be particularly useful if you don’t play super regularly, and want to get caught up.

The next rules change for Warhammer 40,000 will be the quarterly balance update, set to be published the week beginning 7 December.

As a reminder, our aim with the cadence for any rules updates is that they be no more than monthly, with most changes limited to clarifications and addressing errors, and any more impactful amends limited to the quarterly balance updates. So unless your army gets a new Codex, you should really only need to check in four times a year for changes that make a substantive difference to your games.

item.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: October Update
item.description: Rules changes for Khazalite Holds, Sons of Behemat, and more.
item.content:encoded:
New rules updates are going live for Warhammer Age of Sigmar – read on to see if they affect your army.

Warhammer Age of Sigmar

Major changes: Khazalite Holds, Sons of Behemat

Minor changes: Ogor Mawtribes, Lumineth Realm-lords, Skaven, Sylvaneth, Nighthaunt

With the advent of new battletomes, a few older rules needed a quick update to stay relevant – namely where keywords were involved. The Khazalite Holds in particular see a lot of older FYRESLAYERS keywords turned into the new GRIMMDRON,* so things like the Fyreslayers Scourge of Aqshy rules can still be used.

As well as having their keywords changed, the Lofnir Drothkeepers Army of Renown has also been rewritten slightly to better fit their new rules. Notably, it now includes an additional way to generate grudge marks when your Magmadroths are killed.

The Sons of Behemat previously struggled to field game-legal 2,000 point Armies of Renown without needing to dip into Auxiliaries, so now they have a new option to field regiments led by Mancrusher Gargants.** This applies for both the Matriarch’s Mob and Stomper Tribe, so now’s a great time to give their new options a go.

Besides these two larger updates, a few fixes and clarifications have been added to several factions, such as the Skaven’s Verminlord Corruptor having its points corrected after a typo in the last update – one that most of you caught onto anyway, but a slip-up nonetheless! Some units like Pyregheists and Ydrilan Riverblades can also now double up their Champions when reinforced, like other, similar warscrolls. If your faction of choice is listed under minor changes, have a quick look for their updates with the New tag (or search for the ✹ icon).

Spearhead

Major changes: None

Minor changes: Daughters of Khaine Heartflayer Troupe, Nighthaunt Slasher Host, Orruk Warclans Swampskulka Gang, Seraphon Sunblood Prowlers

This is one of the largest Spearhead updates we’ve had for a while, with a handful of ability clarifications that add the ‘Once Per Turn (Army)’ condition to bring them in line with other factions. Otherwise, it’s business as usual in the Spearhead arena, so get out into the City of Ash and show those scuttling Skaven miscreants what for.

Download the latest changes, enjoy your battles in the Mortal Realms, and if you have anything you need answered, make sure to send your questions to AoSFAQ@gwplc.com.

item.title: Warhammer Day – Chaos Champions through the ages
item.description: Take a look back at the heroes of the Dark Gods over the years.
item.content:encoded:
Warhammer Day is this Saturday, and this year’s celebratory miniature – available in stores this weekend – is a majestic Darkoath Warqueen from the Mortal Realms, her Oath Fulfilled. 

This stunning new depiction of a mortal champion of Chaos made some of the… shall we say more seasoned members of the team misty-eyed with nostalgia, so we decided to take a wander down the eightfold path of memory lane and look at Chaos Champions of bygone ages.

Chaos was present from the very beginning of Warhammer Fantasy Battles in 1983, but it was the 1990s that ushered in a plethora of new Champion models directly themed to each of the gods. This was the start of an iterative process that led to the distinct Chaos factions that exist now in the Age of Sigmar. Over the years, the style of each god’s followers was refined across multiple editions and releases, to where we are now.*

Khorne

Nurgle

Slaanesh

Tzeentch

Chaos Undivided

Of course, not all mortal followers of Chaos worship one specific god. Many of them are into Chaos in all its undivided glory,** and the aesthetic of these Champions has also evolved, with both Warhammer: The Old World and Warhammer Age of Sigmar bringing their own twists to the formula in recent years.

The Everchosen

We would be remiss not to mention the greatest Warhammer champion of them all – Archaon. He and his trusty mount Dorghar have experienced their own evolution that echoes that of the wider Chaos faction. 

Darkoath

Warhammer Age of Sigmar, as well as allowing for more detailed explorations of the god-dedicated forces, also opened up space to expand on the Marauders archetype, turning them from a couple of units that followed in the wake of their armoured pals to a fully fleshed-out subfaction of chieftains and Warqueens… which brings us back to Oath Fulfilled. 

Head to your local Warhammer store this Saturday, 31 October, to join in the Warhammer Day celebrations and pick up your very own Oath Fulfilled – with all those textures, we reckon she’s the perfect miniature to try the new Warhammer Tone Pro range on. 

store finder

* Okay, not all of these specific aesthetics have survived – sorry, big hand guy.

** And who can blame them? Some days you want blood and skulls, and others you just fancy a change…

item.title: New battleforce boxes revealed for Warhammer Age of Sigmar
item.description: Start a new collection or expand your existing army.
item.content:encoded:
We’ve seen this year’s crop of Warhammer 40,000 battleforce boxes, and now it’s time to reveal the ones for Warhammer Age of Sigmar.

Stormcast Eternals: Annihilation Host

  • Lord-Commander Bastian Carthalos

  • Lord-Relictor

  • Lord-Celestant

  • 3 Praetors

  • 6 Annihilators

  • 3 Annihilators with Meteoric Grandhammers

Crush Sigmar’s enemies with an unstoppable force of heavy Stormcast infantry, led by the peerless Lord-Commander Bastian Carthalos. Your opponents will know what hit them, and it’ll be a bunch of devastating (war)hammers.

Cities of Sigmar: Knights of Hammerhal

  • Tahlia Vedra, Lioness of the Parch

  • Freeguild Cavalier-Marshal

  • 10 Freeguild Cavaliers

Tahlia Vedra leads a powerful cavalry charge through the gates of your Castelite formation, flanked by the thundering hooves of the Freeguild Cavaliers. They’re speed, power, and style all in one package – perfect for the centrepiece to a wider army.

Maggotkin of Nurgle: Plaguesworn Host

  • Harbinger of Decay

  • Lord of Blights

  • 3 Sloven Knights

  • 5 Putrid Blightkings

  • 10 Rotswords

  • 14 Pox-Wretches

  • 6 Mire Kelpies

Muster a diverse and potent force of Nurgle’s finest plague-bringers with the Plaguesworn Host, which includes a healthy* mix of tough champions, swarming creatures, and mobile cavalry. It’s a solid core around which you can expand a greater Maggotkin of Nurgle army, be it with daemons, larger monsters, or even more resilient infantry.

Orruk Warclans: Grunta Stampede

  • Tuskboss on Maw-Grunta (can alternatively be built as Maw-Grunta Gouger or Maw-Grunta with Hakkin' Krew)

  • Maw-Grunta Gouger (can alternatively be built as Tuskboss on Maw-Grunta or Maw-Grunta with Hakkin' Krew)

  • 6 Gore-Gruntas

Ironjaw Orruks are difficult to stop at the best of times, and become downright wrecking balls when mounted on the back of ornery beasts known as gruntas.** Two big ‘uns riding larger Maw-Gruntas are your hammers, with the (relatively) smaller gore-grunta cavalry stampeding in their wake.

Nighthaunt: Court of the Undying King

  • Nagash, Supreme Lord of the Undead

  • 2 Dreadblade Harrows

  • 10 Dreadscythe Harridans

  • 10 Bladegheist Revenants

  • 10 Grimghast Reapers

Every soul in the Mortal Realms belongs to the Great Necromancer by right, and if the living need convincing of this inalienable fact, the Court of the Undying King will demonstrate it at the end of a spectral blade. Such is the power of Nagash!

Slaves to Darkness: Legion of Damnation

  • Chaos Lord on Daemonic Mount

  • 5 Chaos Chosen

  • 3 Varanguard

  • 5 Chaos Knights

  • 10 Chaos Warriors

The armoured legions of the Varanspire march on the lands of Order, Death, and Destruction, led by a fierce-eyed Chaos Lord. This elite warband is the equal of any force in the Mortal Realms, and wouldn’t dare disappoint the Grand Marshal of the Apocalypse, so you’re in safe hands.

These battleforce boxes will be available for pre-order soon, so keep an eye out for their arrival in our Sunday Preview articles over the next few weeks to learn exactly when. They’re a great starting point for a new foray into the Mortal Realms, and make an excellent gift for the truly special Warhammer fans in your life.***

* For a given value of ‘healthy’ – this is Nurgle after all.
** Or ‘big pigs’ as they’re affectionately known in the Warhammer Community office.
*** Or even as a present for yourself!

In the fourth installment of the legendary Warhammer 40,000 real-time strategy game series, you can take control of four factions – the Space Marines of the Blood Ravens and Dark Angels, Orks, Necrons, and Adeptus Mechanicus – across four campaigns comprising more than 70 thrilling missions.


In addition to the campaigns, there’s a Skirmish mode, with dozens of customisable settings, four game types, and support for up to five AI opponents, where you can hone your skills before taking the battle online across 30 multiplayer maps.

The Last Stand

Fan-favourite co-op survival mode The Last Stand is back, where you and two allies must hold the line against relentless waves of enemies. Choose from five heroes and assemble your strike force of companion units, bringing new layers of strategic depth to every run.

Whichever mode you like to play, the enhanced Painter tool means you can make every army your own. Choose from dozens of presets or create your own schemes with choices of colours, decals, and wargear – for the first time, you have complete creative control to paint your units’ armour and equipment piece-by-piece.

Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is due for release on 3 December 2026, but if you can’t wait until then, the Commander Edition gives players early access three days ahead of the main release. Pre-order either edition now to get a 10% discount, and prepare to begin the fight for Kronus anew.

item.title: New Battleforce boxes revealed for Warhammer 40,000
item.description: Easily start a new army or grow an existing one.
item.content:encoded:
Christmas is quickly approaching – see what Warhammer 40,000 Battleforce boxes you’ll be able to pick up this festive season.

Space Marines: Indomitus Task Force

  • Captain In Terminator Armour

  • Chaplain

  • Redemptor Dreadnought

  • 5 Terminators 

  • 5 Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs

  • 10 Intercessors

The Indomitus Task Force gives you a versatile core to base a Space Marines army around, and includes a little bit of everything Warhammer armies need – shooting, fighting, and durability.

Chaos Knights: Helhunt Lance

  • Knight Ruinator (can alternatively be built as Knight Abominant, Knight Rampager, or Knight Desecrator)

  • 4 War Dog Stalkers (can alternatively be built as War Dog Brigands or War Dog Karnivores)

Dominate the battlefield by sending your tough and terrifying Chaos Knight up the middle of the battlefield while nimble War Dogs snap at the flanks. Just make sure to protect your big guy, and you’ll be stomping corpse-worshippers in no time.

Orks: Armoured Blitzmob

  • Warboss In Mega Armour

  • Battlewagon (can alternatively be built as a Gunwagon)

  • Deff Dread 

  • 3 Meganobz

  • 10 Ork Boyz

Load your Meganobz and Warboss into a Gunwagon and blast them up the field in double-quick time, before unloading everything into your opponent’s face at point-blank range. Build it as a Battlewagon, and you can even fit all 10 of the Boyz in at the same time.

Space Wolves: Champions of Fenris

  • Logan Grimnar

  • Arjac Rockfist

  • 15 Wolf Guard Terminators

Unleash Fenris’ finest with a mass of powerful Wolf Guard Terminators, led by the Great Wolf himself and his personal champion. It’s a force as blunt and savage as the Space Wolves themselves, and a terrifying prospect for any enemy.

Blood Angels: Angelus Assault Force

  • Commander Dante 

  • Blood Angels Chaplain with Jump Pack

  • Death Company Brutalis Dreadnought

  • 3 Sanguinary Guard

  • 5 Death Company Marines with Jump Packs

  • Blood Angels Upgrade Frame

The Blood Angels love a thunderous flight into the thick of the melee, and the Angelus Assault Force gives you units you need to crash down on your foes. All of your infantry hurtle in from above, while the enemy is rightly distracted by a rampaging Brutalis Dreadnought rapidly charging towards them.

Chaos Space Marines: Cult of Destruction

  • Warpsmith

  • Defiler

  • Venomcrawler

  • 2 Obliterators

  • 5 Havocs

  • 3 Mutilators

Heavy weapons and hulking daemon engines are a particular favourite of the Iron Warriors, but you can use this Battleforce to represent any Chaos warband. After all, who in their right mind would turn down a Defiler, especially one flanked by some of the toughest and deadliest infantry this side of the Great Rift?

Necrons: Disciples of the Nekrosor

  • C'tan Shard of the Nightbringer

  • Nekrosor Ammentar

  • 3 Ophydian Destroyers

  • Canoptek Doomstalker

  • 10 Necron Warriors

  • 3 Canoptek Scarab Swarms

Nekrosor Ammentar and his collection of Nightbringer C’tan Shards made an incredible mess around Ultramar and now have their sights set on the rest of the galaxy. Two powerful centrepiece miniatures surrounded by some Necrons mainstays is ideal for reclaiming your lost empire.

If you fancy picking up one of these Battleforce boxes for yourself, or as a Christmas gift for your Warhammer-inclined friends or family, they’ll be available for pre-order soon. Keep checking in with us to be the first to learn exactly when. And stay tuned to find out what’s on offer for Warhammer Age of Sigmar and Warhammer: The Horus Heresy.
